text.content:
The largest Crystal Sphere of all, the Abyss glares across the Astral Sea like a sick eye. It holds countless mutable, nightmarish worlds adrift in glowing storms, and its natives serve the Ruinous Powers, held in check only by the fortress-world Cadia, built over the sole Portal Relay leading out. Ships sometimes slip past the sphere's wall, but its wild currents nearly guarantee death for anyone the Chaos gods do not favour. Inside, the Abyss is far bigger than it looks, a warp-knotted space that may have no end.

Physics and magic shift from region to region, sometimes within a few steps. Many places are survivable for an Exalt with some sorcery, yet wanderers eventually reach somewhere lethal: zones that erase memory, rot flesh, or slowly bend the mind toward the local power. Most of the sphere is a garish, toxic nebula lit by small scattered stars, with planets orbiting them or drifting free. Being pure warp, it has no Umbra; Umbral travel accomplishes nothing and incorporeal beings become solid. Survival favours quick, instinctive decisions over careful preparation.

Because the Warp bleeds directly into it, the whole Abyss effectively lies within the Umbra, so Ghosts, Elementals and Daemons swarm here in far greater numbers than in any healthier sphere. No mortal sentient species is native. The few @UUID[Compendium.dtd40k.races.Item.dtdRaceTiefling0]{Tiefling} residents are usually newly made, pilgrims transformed by immersing themselves in raw warp power, and most of these fresh Tieflings die before they ever find a way back out.

Cadia is a planet-sized stack of fortifications, its deepest layers many millennia old, sealing the only reliable exit. Its ruler, Gerrard Inkheart, has repelled fourteen breakout attempts. Enforcers bless those heading in and screen those returning, and a civilian economy supplying the garrison fills its three-dimensional maze. @UUID[Compendium.dtd40k.deities.Item.dtdDa18240d72ec4]{Khorne} holds the Brass Citadel, his skull throne ringed by a moat of boiling blood and bone-strewn plains. Malal's Battlefield turns visitors' own cherished things against them, with the Tumor, a heap of doomsday weapons, at its core.

Nurgle's Garden is a rotting forest of flies and spore-fungi around his crumbling Mansion and ocean-sized cauldron. The Palace of @UUID[Compendium.dtd40k.deities.Item.dtdD4cd53b93a093]{Slaanesh} lies past six worlds of escalating temptation, ending in a bliss that kills the idle; seeing the god enslaves the soul. The Maze of @UUID[Compendium.dtd40k.deities.Item.dtdD742eca5b0cae]{Tzeentch} threads hidden paths through the whole sphere around the Impossible Fortress and its Hidden Library. The Coffin of @UUID[Compendium.dtd40k.deities.Item.dtdD5f8c6c4a40a4]{Tiamat}, where her fallen soul stained the Abyss, is ruled by a council of renegade Dragons over @UUID[Compendium.dtd40k.races.Item.dtdRaceDragonbor]{Dragonborn} and enslaved lesser races.

Story Master only: adventure seeds for this sphere.

Smugglers are hauling out bizarre artifacts that defy physics and magic, perhaps solidified warp energy, and selling them for fortunes; are they a harbinger of something worse? Cultists of a Chaos god are dragging a living enemy of their patron through the Abyss for sacrifice, and success would fuel a new assault that Cadia is not ready to withstand.

An abandoned, unguarded second Portal Relay has turned up near the Abyss; reactivating it would open a back door for the warp hordes. Meanwhile, Cadia's ancient black pylons, each unique and of unknown origin, dampen warp energy and magic around them, and nobody understands how or why.
